title: [Optional] Local Development Setup
summary: Optional text guide for running the module's React projects locally with Node, VS Code and Vite instead of CodeSandbox.

concepts.heading: Prerequisites
points: Node.js (LTS version) and VS Code installed, and basic comfort with a terminal. The instructor still recommends CodeSandbox for following the videos; local work means adapting differences from the video code.
Each lesson ships a downloadable zip you can use for the starter code.

concepts.heading: Local workflow with Vite
points: Scaffold the project with npm create vite@latest, pick the React framework and the JavaScript variant, then cd into the project.
npm install fetches dependencies into node_modules; npm run dev starts the Vite dev server, which recompiles and reloads on every save.
Open the printed local address (typically http://localhost:5173/) in the browser.

code_examples.caption: Create and run a local React app with Vite
code_examples.code:
npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev
# open http://localhost:5173/

task.name: Optional local React setup
task.starting_point: Node LTS and VS Code installed
task.goal: Run a Vite React app locally
steps: Open a terminal in the folder where the project should live.
Run the Vite scaffold command, accept the install prompt, choose React then JavaScript.
cd into the new folder and run npm install.
Run npm run dev and open the local URL shown.
task.expected_result: Default Vite + React page served at localhost:5173 that hot-reloads on edits.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.05 Introduction to JSX and Babel/my-react-app

pitfalls: (Extra) Newer npm versions need the extra -- before --template for the flag to reach the template; without it npm may swallow the flag and the CLI asks for a framework interactively.
(Extra) The reference repo's later lessons are Vite projects (src/main.jsx, src/App.jsx, index.html with a div#root), matching this setup.
